zh: 好的，Stored 的存在意义，就是为互联网上另外三分之二的商务拉平与 Amazon Prime 之间的竞争环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we look out there, we think that Amazon's product really is delivery.
zh: 当我们放眼外面时，我们认为 Amazon 的产品其实就是配送。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what all other merchants struggle to achieve.

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's what keeps all of us as consumers going to their website to check out instead of independent merchants.

speaker: Unknown
en: So we really see ourselves as the physical intelligence layer combining all the fulfillment and delivery, all of the commerce software, and all of the applied robotics and AI to achieve Amazon level delivery costs, speeds, and consumer experiences.
zh: 所以我们真正把自己看作物理智能层，把所有的履约和配送、所有的商务软件、所有的应用机器人技术和 AI 结合起来，达到 Amazon 级别的配送成本、速度和消费者体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for people that aren't aware, you recently had a milestone of funding and growth.
zh: 那么对于不了解情况的人来说，你最近在融资和增长上达到了一个里程碑。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where are we at with the business?
zh: 业务的进展怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And over the last four years alone, we've 10X the business in terms of scale and revenue in both volume.
zh: 而且仅在过去四年里，我们的业务在规模、收入和交易量上都增长了 10 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's a lot of fueling that future growth where there's so much of an advantage of scale.
zh: 所以这是在为未来的增长补充大量燃料，因为规模优势实在太大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Scale drives economics.
zh: 规模驱动经济性。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also drives density.
zh: 它也驱动密度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's really what builds the moat in delivery, enabling Amazon level speeds and costs.
zh: 而这正是构筑配送护城河的关键，实现 Amazon 级别的速度和成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So continuing to press on the gas hard with scale.
zh: 所以我们要继续在规模上狠狠踩油门。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also announced stored labs along with it, which is very much an application of all of the latest robotics, AI, drones, but also a data foundry actually training the robotics in reverse.
zh: 我们还随之宣布了 stored labs，它很大程度上是所有最新机器人技术、AI、无人机的应用，同时也是一家真正反向训练机器人的数据工厂。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're really excited about how really all the new technology is enabling a vertically integrated industrial business like us to just keep separating our moat from the existing industry we live in.
zh: 所以我们非常兴奋的是，所有这些新技术如何让像我们这样垂直整合的工业企业，能够不断拉开我们与所处现有行业之间的护城河。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's get into that because robotics is super hot right now.
zh: 我们来聊聊这个，因为机器人技术现在非常火。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's flying.
zh: 它在腾飞。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like become the age of robotics.
zh: 就像是进入了机器人时代。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is now the time to go hard on that?
zh: 为什么现在是全力投入的时机？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, if you really look back over history, a lot of the problem with robotics is kind of the dumb robots where if anything goes wrong, if any variable is changed, they can't succeed in that environment anymore.
zh: 是的，如果你真正回顾历史，机器人技术的很多问题在于那种“笨机器人”——一旦出任何差错，一旦任何变量发生变化，它们就无法再在那个环境中成功了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you have a operationally complex environment where every minute or hour could be...
zh: 所以如果你有一个运营上复杂的环境，每一分钟或每一小时都可能是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Hundreds of thousands of dollars or more of productivity, that traditional robotic operation can be quite risky.
zh: 几十万美元甚至更多的生产力，那么传统的机器人运营可能会相当有风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so now you're getting to this point of agentic robotics where you're having robotics that are building real-world models that can see videos for very brief times and learn how to self-heal and get back on track.
zh: 现在你正在进入这种智能体机器人技术的阶段，机器人正在构建真实世界模型，可以在很短的时间内看视频，学会自我修复并回到正轨。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's say you get a slightly different size or form factor in a unit in a fulfillment center.
zh: 比如说，履约中心里的一个货品尺寸或形态略有不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does all of a sudden that go down until IT can show up in code or do something different?
zh: 它是会突然停摆，直到 IT 人员出现改代码或做些别的什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or does the robot learn on the fly with one worker walking up and holding it for three seconds and showing them how to put it in the box?
zh: 还是机器人能现场学习，一个工人走过来，拿着它三秒钟，展示怎么把它放进箱子？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's really where robotics is going and why now is such a moment for it.
zh: 所以这就是机器人技术的发展方向，也是为什么现在是一个重要时刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yet at the same time, if you look back through history and if you study kind of the Teslas and SpaceX's of the world, the whole process and equation is how do you go from refining your processes physically and operationally to then software and kind of repeat that loop over and over again?
zh: 但与此同时，如果你回顾历史，研究一下那些 Tesla 和 SpaceX 式的公司，整个流程和公式就是：如何先在物理和运营上打磨你的流程，然后再到软件，并不断重复这个循环？

speaker: Unknown
en: And only then can you really get the advancement you want in hardware because now you're applying it and really hard coding whatever that process was.
zh: 也只有到那时，你才能真正在硬件上获得你想要的进步，因为现在你正在应用它，并把那个流程真正硬编码下来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if it was under optimized, you're going to fall behind now in a hard coded way.
zh: 所以如果它之前优化不足，你现在就会以一种硬编码的方式落后。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's really the issue with robotics in today's world is a lot of the physical world out there that needs these robots doesn't have the basis of that
zh: 这就是当今机器人领域真正的问题所在，因为外面很多需要这些机器人的物理世界并不具备那样的基础，

speaker: Unknown
en: Best in class process or vertically integrated software to go apply the robot.
zh: 即一流流程或垂直整合的软件来去应用机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's kind of the chasm that robotics is going to have to cross in the period ahead now that they are getting more agentic and self-healing as well.
zh: 所以这就是机器人领域在前方必须跨越的鸿沟，尤其是在它们正变得更加具备智能体特性、更能够自我修复的当下。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what are the typical data points are you collecting through robotics that inform the software and back and forth?
zh: 那么，你们通过机器人采集哪些典型的数据点来反馈给软件、形成来回迭代？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, for us, we process about 8 billion operational data points a year, and that could be anything from how to place a piece of inventory in the network to how to plan for certain consumer demand to how a unit is picked in the facility with labeling on the hands so that they can learn all of these different picking and packing patterns.
zh: 是的，对我们来说，我们每年处理大约 80 亿个运营数据点，这些数据可以是任何东西，从如何把一件库存放置到网络中，到如何规划某些消费者需求，再到一件货在设施里是如何被拣选的——在手部做标注，这样它们就能学习所有这些不同的拣选和打包模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's also post-deployment training, which is videos of the robots after they've actually gone live to show those errors and to help them keep learning
zh: 还有部署后的训练，也就是机器人在实际上线之后的视频，用来展示那些错误并帮助它们持续学习

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's really a ton of data that goes into a business like Stored.
zh: 所以像 Stored 这样的业务，真的有海量的数据投入其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when we're processing about 100 million packages a year to about a third of US households now, almost $20 billion of GMV, that's really one of the most data rich environments that all of these labs and robotics companies are trying to either simulate and learn.
zh: 当我们每年处理大约 1 亿个包裹、覆盖美国大约三分之一的家庭、GMV 接近 200 亿美元时，这真的是所有实验室和机器人公司都在试图模拟和学习的、数据最丰富的环境之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why we have this
zh: 这也是为什么我们拥有这个

speaker: Unknown
en: Not only head start in the e-commerce and logistics industry that we sit in, but also have such an advancement in the robotics in the early phase with these partnerships with leading companies and labs deploying across the stored network because of that data rich environment where let's say you deploy a camera to do the post deployment training on a robot.
zh: 不仅是在我们所处的电商和物流行业里的先发优势，而且在机器人早期阶段也有如此大的领先，通过与领先公司和实验室的合作，在 Stored 网络中部署——正是因为这个数据丰富的环境。比如说，你部署一个摄像头来对机器人做部署后的训练。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, because of our software, we also know in that video, what's the exact dimensions and weight of the box?
zh: 那么，因为我们的软件，我们还在那个视频里知道，这个箱子的精确尺寸和重量是多少？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where's the weight if it's placed?
zh: 如果它被放置了，重量在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's going to have balance difference because of the pack out process.
zh: 因为打包流程，它会有平衡上的差异。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you can enrich these videos with not only labeling of the hands, but that level of vertically integrated data, the learning is just so much faster.
zh: 而当你不仅能用手部标注、还能用那种垂直整合的数据来丰富这些视频时，学习的速度就会快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have to ask this.
zh: 我必须问一下这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a selfish question because they're so popular now and creating a lot of media buzz.
zh: 这是个自私的问题，因为它们现在太火了，制造了很多媒体热度。

speaker: Unknown
en: But do humanoid robotics belong in the factory?
zh: 但是人形机器人属于工厂吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or in a manufacturing warehouse, literally anywhere.
zh: 还是制造业仓库，实际上任何地方？

speaker: Unknown
en: Over time, I think that you'll see 2x plus efficiency output in manufacturing and robotic environments due to really all these different form factors of robots.
zh: 随着时间推移，我认为你会看到制造业和机器人环境中 2 倍以上的效率产出，这得益于各种不同形态的机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think humanoids are the most eye capturing when you look at a video of it as a consumer or just a human and you see this thing.
zh: 我认为人形机器人是最抓眼球的，当你作为消费者或者只是一个人类看到它的视频、看到这个东西的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's really what gets the attention.
zh: 这才是真正吸引注意力的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's a lot of different applications of them because
zh: 但它们有很多不同的应用场景，因为

speaker: Unknown
en: The history was that you could kind of either have like a mounted arm that would pick things or something on the ground like a Kiva that would move things, not two and one.
zh: 历史上是，你要么有一个固定安装的机械臂来抓取东西，要么有地面上的东西比如 Kiva 来移动物品，而不是二合一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you don't actually have to have legs for a robot to move on the ground.
zh: 其实，机器人在地面上移动并不一定需要腿。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't literally have to look like a human to have the same level of, it actually should not look like a human if you want to maximize dexterity.
zh: 它并不非得看起来像人类才能拥有同等的——实际上，如果你想最大化灵巧性，它就不应该看起来像人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think humanoids are interesting, but very much stuck in the pilot phase.
zh: 所以我认为人形机器人很有意思，但很大程度上还卡在试点阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're seeing a lot of advancement in different levels of robotics as well.
zh: 你也看到机器人在不同层面上的很多进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Turns out humans are very inefficient form factors.
zh: 事实证明，人类是非常低效的形态。

speaker: Unknown
en: That might be the quote of the day.
zh: 这可能是今日金句。

speaker: Unknown
en: So stored has grown by also acquisition and roll ups are kind of a hot thing as well.
zh: 所以 Stored 也通过收购实现增长，而滚动式收购现在也是个热门话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So are you a roll up?
zh: 那么你们是滚动式收购吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about acquisitions?
zh: 你们如何看待收购？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the growth of the business kind of pan out to in the next couple of years?
zh: 未来几年业务的增长大概会是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, when we started this business, we toured warehouses, fulfillment centers, and we were thinking about, should we build the software layer on top to orchestrate a prime-like network for other brands?
zh: 是的，当我们创办这家业务时，我们参观了很多仓库、履约中心，我们在思考，是否应该在上面构建软件层，为其他品牌编排一个类 Prime 的网络？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we kind of got stuck on this problem of, well, if you walk in the average warehouse, many of them are still doing paper-based picking where a worker prints out, go build an order of these units and walks around the facility, either from memory or from just looking around at cards and aisles in the facility.
zh: 而我们卡在了这个问题上：嗯，如果你走进一个普通的仓库，很多仍在做基于纸张的拣选，工人打印出来，去把这些货组成一个订单，然后在设施里走来走去，要么凭记忆，要么只是四处看着卡片和设施里的通道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how can you really expect prime level delivery, drones, and all the advancement in robotics if the industry they're going into is so far behind?
zh: 那么你怎么能真正期待 Prime 级别的配送、无人机以及机器人领域的一切进步，如果它们要进入的行业落后这么多？

speaker: Unknown
en: So from the earliest day, we really chose to vertically integrate and say, well, we're gonna be both the software and the physical behind this to power that prime-like delivery for everyone else so that when we build this best-in-class software, we can actually apply it to the physical service it's behind.
zh: 所以从最早的时候起，我们就真的选择垂直整合，说，好吧，我们要同时做这背后的软件和实体，为其他所有人提供类 Prime 的配送，这样当我们构建这套一流的软件时，我们就能真正把它应用到它背后的实体服务上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's really what's changed.
zh: 而这真的是改变所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back when we started, physical wasn't really in vogue.
zh: 在我们起步的时候，实体并不是流行的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't the thing to do.
zh: 那不是大家在做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you're seeing these new applied kind of roll-up companies, holdings companies, and more saying, wait a second, I can build the best accounting software or whatever it may be, but if the accounting industry is slow to adopt, what if I go accrue all that advantage into my own company and my own accounting service where I own the data, the customer, and the software and AI powering this?
zh: 而现在你看到这些新的应用型滚动式收购公司、控股公司等等在说，等一下，我可以构建最好的会计软件或随便什么软件，但如果会计行业采用缓慢呢？如果我把所有这些优势都累积进我自己的公司、我自己的会计服务，让我拥有数据、客户以及驱动这一切的软件和 AI 呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so really, if you think about Stored, our secret sauce is this vertically integrated software, but how it's applied to real world operations.
zh: 所以真的，如果你想想 Stored，我们的秘诀就是这种垂直整合的软件，以及它如何被应用到现实世界的运营中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the flywheel of this business is that the more volume you serve, the lower cost, the faster speed, and the greater trust.
zh: 而这个业务的飞轮在于，你服务的量越大，成本就越低、速度就越快、信任度就越高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if the average business out in the US is delivering for $15 plus a package in five to six business days, while Amazon's delivering for $5 a package in one to two days, if not even half a day, that's the fundamental gap that exists.
zh: 如果美国普通企业配送一个包裹要 15 美元以上、需要 5 到 6 个工作日，而亚马逊 1 到 2 天、甚至半天就能以每包裹 5 美元配送，那就是存在的根本差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the race to scale and spin that flywheel to level the playing field is really on and we're in the lead.
zh: 所以扩大规模、转动那个飞轮以拉平竞争环境的竞赛 really 正在进行，而且我们处于领先。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when we look at acquisitions,
zh: 所以当我们看收购时，

speaker: Unknown
en: We've actually been probably the most efficient on cost and also the highest outcome on uplift to these businesses because you're buying both density in the network and volume, but you're also applying your unit economics and your software throughout this business.
zh: 我们实际上可能是成本上最高效的，同时也是对这些业务的提升效果上产出最高的，因为你既买到了网络中的密度和量，同时你也在把这个业务的单位经济模型和软件应用贯穿其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in most of the deals we've done, we've seen five to seven or even more times uplift of the efficiency and therefore profitability of these businesses in extremely short time horizons.
zh: 所以在我们完成的大多数交易中，我们在极短的时间内就看到了这些业务的效率、因而盈利能力 5 到 7 倍甚至更高的提升。

en: Damn.

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not 19 anymore?

speaker: Unknown
en: Not 19 anymore.
zh: 不是 19 岁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's about 10 years ago.
zh: 那大概是 10 年前的事了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're now evolved and mature.
zh: 你现在成熟进化了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you started in logistics there.
zh: 所以你当时从物流领域起步。

speaker: Unknown
en: What made you get so interested in logistics so early on?
zh: 是什么让你这么早就对物流这么感兴趣？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really, it's easier going backwards when you kind of look at being an entrepreneur, but a lot of times, probably a few of you around here, I'll pull out my phone and show my real live eBay account where it shows members since 2003.
zh: 说实话，当你回头看创业经历时，倒着讲更容易，但很多时候，可能这里的几位，我会拿出手机展示我真实的 eBay 账户，上面显示 2003 年就注册成为会员了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was very young selling products online really to just...
zh: 我很小的时候就在网上卖东西，其实只是为了……

speaker: Unknown
en: Pay for anything in my life and get involved.
zh: 支付我生活中的各种开销并参与其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what happened was I saw the reviews go from be about the product you sold and I did or didn't like that product to just about the shipping and kind of post-click experience.
zh: 后来我发现评价从关于你卖的商品、我是否喜欢那个商品，变成了只关于物流运输和点击后的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just how fast was it?
zh: 就是有多快？

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the customer service?
zh: 客服怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the returns?
zh: 退货怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: And kind of trace that to the rise of Amazon and Prime and consumers now believing, well, I can get anything online.
zh: 然后把这追溯到 Amazon 和 Prime 的崛起，消费者现在相信，我可以在网上买到任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The difference is who actually provides that post-click experience.
zh: 区别在于谁真正提供那种点击后的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that was really the kind of trend I was looking at.
zh: 所以那才是我真正关注的那种趋势。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was a student at Georgia Tech.
zh: 当时我是佐治亚理工学院的学生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my kind of funny Teal Fellows story is I actually dropped out more than a year before I got the Teal Fellowship.
zh: 我那段有点好笑的 Teal 学者故事是，实际上我在拿到 Teal 奖学金一年多之前就退学了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was almost in arrears, but still was quite validating to my parents and my family.
zh: 所以几乎是事后补发的，但对我的父母和家人来说仍然是非常大的认可。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think Jake joked about it earlier that there's a lot of different college startups you think of.
zh: 我记得 Jake 前面还开玩笑说，大学创业公司有很多种你想象得到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember our first kind of angel investor when we were students, they were like, most college students I know start a dating app to meet someone faster or an on-demand beer company to get drunk faster.
zh: 我记得我们还是学生时的第一位天使投资人，他们说，我认识的大多数大学生创业，要么是做个约会软件让自己更快脱单，要么是做个按需送啤酒的公司让自己更快喝醉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, why are you doing logistics?
zh: 像，你们为什么要做物流？

speaker: Unknown
en: We're really just solving a problem we've seen ourselves in that if we look out at the world, it almost seems like too obvious.
zh: 我们真的只是在解决我们自己亲身体会到的问题，放眼这个世界，这看起来几乎是显而易见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you ask any consumer, what's the best delivery service?
zh: 比如，你问任何消费者，最好的配送服务是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do you want to shop online?
zh: 你想在哪里网购？

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer is Amazon.
zh: 答案是 Amazon。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, why is no one doing that for the other two thirds of the internet across e-commerce?
zh: 那么，为什么没有人为互联网上另外三分之二的电商做同样的事？

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the biggest lesson you learned from the Teal Fellowship?
zh: 你从 Teal 奖学金中学到的最大一课是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they really impress upon you what is your right to win and essentially build the biggest company possible, i.e.
zh: 我认为他们真的会让你深刻思考什么是你的制胜权利，本质上是打造尽可能大的公司，也就是，

speaker: Unknown
en: build a monopoly over time.
zh: 随时间建立垄断。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that their whole goal is that that's really what you should strive for, not that it should exist in the sense you want to win your category.
zh: 我认为他们的整个目标就是，那才是你真正应该追求的，不是说垄断本身应该存在，而是你想赢下你的品类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think they really dug into that precision of why will this win in the long term?
zh: 所以他们真的深挖了那种精确性：为什么这会在长期获胜？

speaker: Unknown
en: And for us, a lot of it comes back to that flywheel where
zh: 对我们来说，很多都回到那个飞轮，

speaker: Unknown
en: It's really hard to catch up to the speed and cost advantage.
zh: 速度和成本优势真的很难被追上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, if the industry's at $15 in five or six days and Amazon's at $5 in a day and now stored as sub $7, $8 and delivering in two days and we can deliver in one day depending on placement.
zh: 再说一次，如果行业水平是 15 美元、五六天，Amazon 是 5 美元一天，而现在我们 stored 是 7、8 美元以下，两天送达，根据 placements 不同我们可以一天送达。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very hard for that industry to catch up.
zh: 那个行业要追上来非常难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as we've spun that flywheel, we can trace our win rate in sales from sub 10% to over 50% because these brands can't find that level of capability elsewhere.
zh: 随着我们转动这个飞轮，我们可以追踪到我们的销售赢单率从不到 10% 提升到超过 50%，因为这些品牌在别处找不到那种水平的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when you're able to articulate why as you get bigger, you actually get better as a company and becomes harder to compete with you and you can move faster at scale.
zh: 所以当你能够清晰地阐述为什么随着你变大，你的公司实际上会变得更好、变得更难被竞争、并且你可以在规模上移动得更快，

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why we're growing faster at scale.
zh: 那就是为什么我们在规模化时反而增长得更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's really what the Teal Fellowship impresses on you and subsequently Founders Fund who led our rounds and joined the cap table.
zh: 我认为这就是 Teal 奖学金真正让你刻在心里的东西，以及随后领投我们轮次并进入股权表的 Founders Fund 也是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: As we close out, I'll make this one quick.
zh: 快结束时了，我快点问这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is your hottest take right now?
zh: 你现在最大胆的观点是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's all this obsession with kind of AI and robotics, whether you're an investor or you're a consumer and you're afraid of how that's going to displace you.
zh: 我觉得现在所有人都在痴迷 AI 和机器人技术，无论你是投资者，还是你是一个害怕自己会被取代的消费者。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I really think that there's a fundamental gap in that.
zh: 而我真的认为这中间存在一个根本性的鸿沟。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think the value is going to keep accruing to the AI and to the robotics.
zh: 我不认为价值会持续累积到 AI 和机器人技术上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it actually accrues to the application layer and to the real world.
zh: 我认为它实际上会积累到应用层和现实世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I believe humans' lives are going to get better.
zh: 所以我相信人类的生活会变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I believe physical businesses like Stored are going to win and get faster and cheaper.
zh: 我相信像 Stored 这样的实体企业会获胜，并且变得更快、更便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And long term, it's actually these super fast growth AI companies and robotics that end up commoditized by how low the cost becomes to replicate them internally across companies and for individuals even.
zh: 而从长远来看，真正会被商品化的反而是这些增长极快的 AI 公司和机器人技术，因为在公司之间、甚至在个人层面复制它们的内部成本会变得如此之低。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Sean, thank you so much.
zh: 好，Sean，非常感谢你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for having me.
zh: 谢谢你们的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, it's Molly.
zh: 嗨，我是 Molly。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you enjoy our interviews, check out our newsletter, sorcery.vc, where we deliver a once a week top deals and tech headlines email, and also go deeper on our podcast interviews.
zh: 如果你喜欢我们的访谈，请查看我们的通讯 sorcery.vc，我们每周发送一封顶级交易和科技头条的邮件，还会对我们的播客访谈做更深入的展开。

speaker: Unknown
en: Subscribe to Sorcery today.
zh: 今天就订阅 Sorcery。

speaker: Unknown
en: And don't forget to subscribe to the podcast on YouTube, Spotify, Apple, or wherever you listen.
zh: 别忘了在 YouTube、Spotify、Apple 或任何你收听的地方订阅这个播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Link in description to sign up.
zh: 报名链接在简介中。
